item.title: Naoshima Art Island: A Day Trip from Okayama — Guide
item.description: Naoshima is a small island in the Seto Inland Sea that has become one of the most celebrated contemporary art destinations on earth. From the 1990s, the Benesse corporation and architect Tadao Ando remade it: concrete museums are sunk into the hillsides so as not to intrude on the landscape, works by Monet, Turrell and De Maria sit in purpose-built chambers, Yayoi Kusama’s spotted pumpkins stand on the piers, and in the village of Honmura old wooden houses have been converted into individual artworks.
